title: You’re stressing about tomorrow… but Jesus already stepped into it.
paragraphs: You’re stressing about tomorrow… but Jesus already stepped into it.
“Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.” — Matthew 6:34
You feel it, don’t you?

That quiet panic.
The “what ifs.”
The weight of things that haven’t even happened yet.

Bills not paid.
Decisions not made.
Outcomes you can’t control.
And your mind runs ahead… like it’s trying to play God.
But listen—Jesus cuts through the noise with one command:
“Do not worry.”

Not because life is easy.
Not because problems aren’t real.
But because you are not alone in tomorrow.
He already stands there.

We worry because we think everything depends on us.
Provision. Protection. The future.
But here’s what we miss…
Worry is a quiet form of unbelief.

It says:
“God, I trust You for yesterday… but not for what’s next.”
And yet Scripture keeps pulling us back:

The same God who fed you yesterday…
The same Savior who carried your sin on the cross…
The same Spirit who woke you up today…
He will not abandon you tomorrow.
This verse isn’t just about anxiety.
It’s about lordship.
Who’s really in control of your future?

Because when Jesus died and rose again, He didn’t just save your soul—
He claimed your tomorrows.

Your unknowns.
Your fears.
Your unfinished stories.
So breathe.

Not shallow.
Not rushed.
Deep.
Then surrender what hasn’t happened yet.
Give it to the One who already wrote the ending in grace.
Type “I trust You, Lord”—not for show, but as surrender.
Because peace isn’t found in control.
It’s found in Christ.
From anxiety to assurance—because Jesus already stands in your tomorrow.
